content:
**Observations:**

- **Plant**: Tomato (compound leaves visible)
- **Affected parts**: Stems and whole plant, uprooted to show crown/root junction
- **Key features**:
  - Extensive **bleaching/blanching of the entire stem** — pale white/cream color along most of the stem length
  - **Dark lesions** visible on the bleached stem tissue
  - **Complete plant collapse/wilt** — fully prostrate
  - Roots appear brown and desiccated
  - Leaves wilted and browning at margins

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Southern_Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*): bleaching primarily at the soil line/crown, white mycelial mat visible at ground level — possible, but bleaching here extends further up the stem
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*): causes water-soaked lesions at stem internodes that rapidly bleach to straw/white color, stem girdling leads to complete collapse. The **extensive straw-white bleaching running along the full stem length** (not confined to soil line), combined with dark lesions on the bleached tissue and full plant collapse, is classic for Sclerotinia stem rot/timber rot
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**: would show unilateral wilt early, internal vascular browning, bird's-eye lesions on fruit — not consistent
- **Verticillium/Fusarium wilt**: internal vascular discoloration, not external stem bleaching of this degree

The hallmark here is the **full-length stem bleaching with a straw/white color and dark lesion overlay**, which most specifically fits Sclerotinia timber rot.
